titre_page: How to add particles and effects in Yop2D? | Yop2D Guide
description: Explosions, fire, smoke, a ship's wake, flash and fade: add visual effects in Yop2D without code, with the Particles object and the [[effet_particules]], [[flash_ecran]] and [[fondu_ecran]] nodes.
h1: How to add particles and effects?
carte: An explosion when you touch an enemy, a trail behind the ship, a screen flash and a fade.
etapes: A {{lang:obj_prefix_particules}} object ({{lang:option.Sillage}}) attached to the character.
{{flash_ecran}} when you get hit, {{fondu_ecran}} between two levels.
blocs: Yop2D makes particles in two ways: the **[[effet_particules]]** node fires a burst all at once (perfect for an explosion), and the **{{lang:obj_prefix_particules}}** object produces them non-stop (fire, smoke, rain, trail…). Other nodes add effects over the whole screen: flash, tint, vignette and fade.
a working game, with a character named **player** that can move;
To see all these effects in action, open the **Effects showcase** example on the Yop2D home screen: one button per effect, with the name of the node to use.
Step 1: an explosion when you touch an enemy
Add **[[effet_particules]]**. As the target, choose **{{lang:noeud_objet_implique_long}}**: it is the enemy the player just touched. {{lang:effet_particules.modele}}: **{{lang:option.Explosion}}**.
Link the three nodes in order, then start the game and touch an enemy: it explodes before disappearing.
**Order matters:** [[effet_particules]] must come **before** [[detruire_objet]]. Once the enemy is destroyed, there is no object left to place the explosion on.

You can change the **color** (for example `#FF40D0` for a magenta explosion) and the **size** (2 = twice as big). Also try {{lang:option.Etincelles}}, {{lang:option.Confettis}} or {{lang:option.Fumee}}.
Step 2: a trail behind the character
Add an object: in the **{{lang:cat_effets}}** category, choose **{{lang:obj_prefix_particules}}**. In the editor it shows as a dotted orange area; in the game it is invisible.
In the inspector, **{{lang:insp_sep_particules}}** section, tap **{{lang:insp_btn_modele_particules}}** and choose **{{lang:option.Sillage}}**.
Still in the inspector, tap the **{{lang:insp_btn_parent_aucun}}** button and choose **player**: the object will follow the character everywhere.
Place it just behind the character, then start the game and move: a long glowing trail follows the character.

Nothing to add in the Blueprint: a {{lang:obj_prefix_particules}} object works on its own as long as **{{lang:insp_cb_particules_actives}}** is checked. To turn it on or off during the game, use the **[[particules_marche]]** node.
**{{lang:option.Pluie}}** or **{{lang:option.Neige}}**: stretch the object across the whole top of the screen.
**{{lang:option.Hyperespace}}** and **{{lang:option.LignesVitesse}}**: to give a feeling of great speed.
Step 3: effects over the whole screen
**[[flash_ecran]]**: a flash of color. For example red, 0.5 seconds, right after the player gets hit.
**[[teinte_ecran]]**: a color over the whole game. Dark blue at 55% for night, and intensity 0 to go back to daytime.
**[[bords_assombris]]**: the edges of the screen get darker, like in a movie.
**[[fondu_ecran]]**: the screen goes black, then comes back.
To move to the next level smoothly (see [the levels guide](guide:niveau-suivant)):
The tint and the vignette stay **under the HUD**: the score and the buttons stay easy to read. The flash and the fade cover the whole screen.
**[[electrocution]]**: lightning crackles around an object, which flashes and shakes. Duration **0** = endless: perfect for an electric trap that warns the player.
**[[arret_sur_image]]**: a very short slow-motion (0.08 seconds) at the moment of impact gives an explosion a lot of punch.
**The explosion doesn't show:** check that [[effet_particules]] is placed **before** [[detruire_objet]].
**The trail doesn't follow the character:** check that the {{lang:obj_prefix_particules}} object has **player** as its parent, and that {{lang:insp_cb_particules_actives}} is checked.
**The particles have the wrong color:** the color “{{lang:insp_couleur_aucune}}” keeps the preset colors; choose a real color to change them.
**The screen stays black:** after a [[fondu_ecran]] {{lang:option.Disparaitre}}, you need a [[fondu_ecran]] {{lang:option.Apparaitre}}.
